name: Sestina
note: Six end-words, no rhyme, and a fixed spiral that retires each word through every position before returning it. You choose six words and then spend thirty-nine lines being driven back to them. Choose words that can change part of speech.
ground: Arnaut Daniel, twelfth century, Provencal. The permutation is a single rule applied six times — take the last, then the first, then the second-to-last, then the second, and so on — and it happens to return to the starting order on the seventh pass, which is why the form is exactly six stanzas long and could not be any other length.
ask: Can at least two of your six words work as more than one part of speech?
